Department 4

Feeder station

Nectar, seed, water, and the plants that bring them in

Hummingbird nectar mixer

Stir in

1 cup

of plain white table sugar. That is the 1 part sugar to 4 parts water mix that matches flower nectar. Warm the water to help it dissolve, then let it cool. No red dye, no honey, no brown or raw sugar.

How often to change nectar
Every 2 days

Cloudy nectar or black specks mean mold. Dump it and scrub the feeder with hot water and a bottle brush. Texas summer heat spoils nectar fast.

Seed and food guide
Black-oil sunflowerThe all-purpose seed. Cardinals, chickadees, titmice, Blue Jays, finches, woodpeckers.
SafflowerCardinals love it. Grackles and squirrels mostly leave it alone.
Nyjer (thistle) in a tube sockAmerican Goldfinches in winter, plus House Finches.
White proso millet on a trayGround feeders: doves, sparrows, towhees. Also draws Painted Buntings in spring.
No-melt suetWoodpeckers, wrens, mockingbirds. Pick a no-melt blend for Texas summers.
Orange halves & grape jellyOrioles during spring and fall migration.
Fresh water, 1–2 in. deepBrings in birds that never touch a feeder, like bluebirds, waxwings, and warblers. Change it every couple of days.
Plant for hummingbirds
  • Turk's cap
  • Flame acanthus
  • Autumn sage (Salvia greggii)
  • Coral honeysuckle (the native one)
  • Firebush (Hamelia patens)
  • Red yucca
  • Shrimp plant & fuchsia in pots
Plant for cardinals & songbirds
  • Yaupon holly (berries all winter)
  • American beautyberry
  • Possumhaw
  • Coneflower & sunflower (leave the seed heads)
  • Dense shrubs for nesting cover
Fall migration tip

Keep nectar feeders up through October and into November. Leaving them up does not keep hummingbirds from migrating, and late travelers coming down the coast need the fuel.
